name: dn-cn-embedded-nul-evades-constraint-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees directoryName is C=US,O=Example,CN=honest.example.com. The leaf subject's CN contains a NUL byte followed by an attacker-chosen suffix (the bytes of 'honest.example.com', then 00, then 'evil.example.com'). RFC 5280 7.1 requires comparison of the full Unicode value, so the leaf's CN is not equal to the constraint's CN and the leaf must be rejected as outside the permitted subtree. Implementations that treat the CN as a C string and truncate at the NUL will see the prefix 'honest.example.com' and incorrectly accept.
references: DEFCON 17 (Marlinspike) 'Null Prefix Attacks Against SSL/TLS Certificates'
notes: The CN is constructed via subject_der_ascii2der to keep the NUL byte unambiguous in the source. The attack vector is real: TLS stacks that fed the CN through C string APIs have shipped this bug (Mozilla NSS, GnuTLS, others). For name-constraint validation, the equivalent risk is a constraint comparator that uses strcmp/strncmp.

certs.subject: C=US,O=Example,CN=Placeholder
certs.subject_der_ascii2der: SEQUENCE { SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.6 } PrintableString { "US" } } } SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.10 } UTF8String { "Example" } } } SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.3 } UTF8String { `686f6e6573742e6578616d706c652e636f6d006576696c2e6578616d706c652e636f6d` } } } }
